                    ### Question
                    In a 68-year-old patient with new onset headache, pain and prolonged morning stiffness in scapular and pelvic girdles of several weeks of evolution that presents unilateral bruising of sudden onset, what treatment among the following would establish before confirming the diagnosis?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Prednisone 10 mg daily v.o.
opb. Methylprednisolone 1 g i.v. daily for three days.
opc. Cyclophosphamide i.v. 1 g / m2.
opd. Infliximab i.v. 3 mg / Kg.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In a 68-year-old patient with new onset headache, prolonged morning stiffness, and unilateral bruising, the clinical picture suggests possible giant cell arteritis or polymyalgia rheumatica. Prednisone is the first-line treatment for these conditions, as it effectively reduces inflammation and improves symptoms. Methylprednisolone may be considered for severe cases but is not the first-line treatment. Cyclophosphamide is not appropriate at this stage, as it is used for more severe autoimmune conditions and not for initial management. Infliximab is also not suitable for acute treatment. Therefore, the best option to establish treatment before confirming the diagnosis is Prednisone 10 mg daily, as it aligns with standard medical consensus for managing suspected inflammatory conditions in this patient demographic.
